study: West/Morton/Herlihy 2016, Achievement Network (ANet) data-driven instruction PD, i3 expansion eval (CEPR Harvard)
eval_evidence: Independent impact evaluation conducted by the Center for Education Policy Research (CEPR) at Harvard University, the i3 independent evaluator, which 'partnered' with ANet; CEPR is not the program developer.
developer_evidence: The PD/support was delivered by Achievement Network's own staff (ANet coaches and ANet staff) — the program organization itself, not the independent evaluators or the school system.
cascade_evidence: Each school was assigned an ANet coach who worked directly with the school leader and data leadership team; ANet staff delivered the program to schools directly (no train-the-trainer hop).
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools were not barred from using their own interim assessments and district data support, so the contrast is ANet over-and-above typical district-led data-driven-instruction efforts (active/contaminated counterfactual).
coaching_evidence: ANet coaches visited schools on average ~17 times per year, but coaching targeted school leaders/data leadership teams in data meetings, not recurring in-class coaching of individual teachers in their classrooms.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention is interim assessments + data platform/reporting + leader/teacher data coaching; only teacher and leader practice changes, no tutoring, pull-out, or student-facing instructional dose.
maturity_evidence: Confirmatory student impacts measured at the end of Year 2 (after a full prior implementation year); schools/teachers had >=1 year of ANet experience by the measurement wave.
